key_insight: RepFusion shows that denoising for text-to-image generation can be moved into a semantically rich representation space, where pretrained multimodal and language priors are much more useful. By aligning visual representations with LLM-friendly structure, the model can generate better without relying on a fully new generative backbone.
problem_solved: Traditional T2I systems use LLMs mainly for text encoding, while the actual denoising/generation happens in separately trained image backbones. This paper addresses the mismatch between powerful pretrained language priors and the latent spaces used for image generation.
method: Use representation autoencoders (RAEs) to transform generation from pixel/image latents into semantically structured visual representations.
Leverage pretrained multimodal priors to guide denoising directly in representation space.
Apply a lightweight alignment strategy inspired by MLLMs, using an MLP projector to connect visual representations with language-model priors.
impact: This approach can make text-to-image systems more compatible with pretrained foundation models, reducing the need to train large denoising backbones from scratch. For practitioners, it suggests a more efficient path to stronger generation quality by reusing existing LLM/MLLM knowledge.
